analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (10 November 2026)
key_insights: US equities rallied on Monday. The S&P 500 had its strongest session since March (+2.35%, 7549.94), the Nasdaq its best day since June (+2.74%), and the Dow rose 2.15%. Advancers outnumbered decliners by nearly 6:1, with the most positive breadth since November 2025.

The AI trade extended Friday's gains on cleaner positioning after last week's aggressive selling. Drivers cited were reports that Anthropic is pushing ahead with an IPO at a valuation around $1.5T and Alphabet's launch of two new TPU chips.

Positive US/Iran diplomatic headlines supported risk appetite. WTI crude settled down 4.4% and back below $90/barrel, extending last week's roughly 13% slide. Trump said further Iran strikes are 'highly unlikely', while Rubio said indirect talks have not been productive.

October core CPI is due Tuesday at 8:30 ET, expected at +0.2% m/m against September's +0.3%. Markets price about an 80% chance of a December Fed hike and 43 bp of hikes through the end of next year. Previews said the report is unlikely to shift Fed expectations unless it comes in unexpectedly soft.
Short-end Treasury yields rose 2-4 bp and the dollar index fell 0.6% on Monday. The US 2-year yield is 4.56%, the 10-year 4.88%, and the 2s10s spread 32 bp.

Nvidia fell 5.7% after the board launched an internal investigation into CEO Huang's relationship with a woman the US deems a Chinese intelligence asset. Analysts are debating whether Huang can remain CEO, note there may be no clear successor, and expect more scrutiny of tech export restrictions to China.
Sector leadership in the US: networking, cybersecurity, small-caps, transports, homebuilders, banks and space outperformed. Energy, managed care, credit cards and China tech lagged.

The NY Fed's October Survey of Consumer Expectations showed one-year inflation expectations at 3.9%, three-year at 3.3% and five-year at 3.0%. Unemployment expectations rose 1.4 pp to 45.3%, the highest since Apr-20, and delinquency expectations rose 1.6 pp to 13.8%.
Fed speakers: Goolsbee said services inflation is beginning to kick up. Barkin said the policy rate may be at or slightly below neutral, with no baseline scenario for the December meeting.

European equities closed higher (Germany +1.7%, France +1.2%, UK +1%). Cyclicals led, with banks, miners and technology on top, and defensives lagged. Luxury stocks stayed weak after October data pointed to weak Chinese consumer demand.

Eurozone inflation accelerated to 4.0% in October. Nagel and Kocher signalled the need for further ECB tightening, and markets price about an 80% chance of a December ECB hike. Citi said a much larger and sustained fall in energy prices is needed to remove a December hike. BofA noted the rate curve shows about 30% probability of March tightening.

Eurozone finance ministers held first talks on succeeding ECB President Lagarde, who leaves in February. The only nominees are Knot and de Cos. EU leaders aim to appoint a successor by the mid-December summit, though it could slip to January.
The ECB is considering a review of banks' data center lending, following a similar BoE move. The EBA chair said EU bank exposure to the overall ICT sector is 4%.

The Eurozone Sentix headline index was 2.4 against consensus 2.1 and a prior 2.7. The expectations index fell to 8.3 from 8.8, the weakest since June 2026. The German headline index rose to -3.3 from -3.6.

European M&A: Crédit Agricole proposed a friendly merger of Banco BPM with Crédit Agricole Italia at a 20% valuation premium (Banco BPM +10.1%). UniCredit (+6.2%) expects to take control of Commerzbank by end-November and raised its FY net profit target to above €11.5B.

Asian equities rose broadly. Japan gained 2.33% and Taiwan's Taiex was much stronger. Taiwan activated a stabilization fund of up to NT$500B and tightened short-selling limits, with similar rescue measures in South Korea. TSMC outperformed on reports it is considering developing advanced memory chips.
China's October PPI rose 5.7% y/y against 5.3% consensus, driven by energy. CPI eased to 0.7% against 0.8% consensus, and core CPI was 0.8% against 0.9% consensus.
The New Zealand election is too close to call. The right bloc (National-ACT-NZ First) leads with 67 seats against 57 for the left bloc, and the final result may be delayed until 27-Nov.

A Nikkei analysis found 112 of 239 Japanese manufacturers (47%) raised FY net profit guidance, adding JPY2.4T to aggregate earnings projected at JPY63.4T. Concerns include AI spending sustainability after the US midterms and fading weak-yen windfalls.
Philippines Q3 GDP grew 2.1% y/y against 3.5% consensus, with October CPI at 7.8%, the worst inflation in Asia since the Iran conflict began.

Notable US single-stock moves: CECO +23.2% on a Q3 beat with orders +234%, Ferguson +13.3% on a beat and raised guidance, Surgery Partners +12.8% after rejecting a $28-a-share UnitedHealth offer, Ionis -23.8% after cutting its TRYNGOLZA sales outlook roughly in half, and Zura Bio -71.5% on a failed phase 2 HS study.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell 5.7% as the board opened an internal investigation into CEO Huang's relationship with a woman the US deems a Chinese intelligence asset. Analysts question whether Huang stays as CEO and note no clear successor.
Oppenheimer upgraded to outperform from perform, citing optimism after the recent earnings report and management conversations. Shares rose 12.7%.
Rothschild & Co Redburn upgraded to neutral from sell. It believes a stronger growth outlook now better supports the stock's premium valuation.
Q3 EPS, revenue and EBITDA beat, with orders +234% and backlog at $2.2B. FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance came in sharply above consensus.
Q3 EPS, EBITDA and revenue all beat, and organic growth was well ahead of estimates. The company raised the low end of its EBITDA margin forecast, and analysts called guidance likely conservative.
Cut FY26 TRYNGOLZA sales outlook roughly in half amid slower adoption. Shares fell 23.8% despite a narrower Q3 loss.
Bloomberg reported UnitedHealth made an unsolicited $28 per share buyout offer, which was rejected. Shares rose 12.8%.
Q3 EPS, EBITDA and FCF beat, but the FY27 EPS outlook was below expectations. It agreed to sell six gas generation assets to LS Power for $4B cash.
Q3 EPS, revenue and EBITDA beat and FY26 EBITDA and cash flow guidance was raised. Power revenue grew 28% q/q and a 76MW data center power agreement was announced.
Q3 EPS, operating income and revenue beat and FY26 guidance was raised, but billings were light. Shares fell 6.2%.
A phase 3 study of Foundayo in obstructive sleep apnea met its primary endpoint. The company plans to file for FDA approval by end-2026.
Announced two new TPU AI chips focused on confidential computing and longer context windows. Shares rose 1.7%.
JPMorgan upgraded SAP to overweight, helping European technology recover.
Reported to have submitted an unsolicited $28 per share buyout offer for Surgery Partners, which was rejected.

earnings_insights: CECO Environmental Q3 (reported): EPS, revenue and EBITDA beat consensus, orders +234%, backlog $2.2B, FY26 orders and cash flow conversion outlooks raised, initial FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance sharply above consensus.
Ferguson Q3 (reported): EPS, EBITDA and revenue beat. It guided FY26 revenue growth of about 7% and raised the low end of its EBITDA margin forecast.
NRG Energy Q3 (reported): EPS, EBITDA and FCF beat. FY26 guidance was largely in line with consensus and the FY27 EPS outlook was below expectations.
Kodiak Gas Services Q3 (reported): EPS, revenue and EBITDA beat. FY26 EBITDA and cash flow guidance raised, and Power revenue grew 28% q/q.
monday.com Q3 (reported): EPS, operating income and revenue beat but billings were light. FY26 revenue and operating income guidance raised and the FCF range narrowed.

Ionis Q3 (reported): loss narrower than expected and revenue sharply ahead on collaboration payments and royalties. The FY26 TRYNGOLZA sales outlook was cut roughly in half and overall revenue guidance reaffirmed.
Roivant FQ2 (reported): earnings better than the Street and R&D expense below consensus.
Turning Point Brands Q3 (reported): earnings and revenue better, FY26 guidance reaffirmed, with a profit headwind from the mix shift to Modern Oral.
Fervo Energy Q3 (reported): EPS better, revenue in line, operating income missed. Q4 capex midpoint guided ahead of estimates.

UniCredit Q3 (reported): net profit +24% y/y to €3.3B on revenue +12% to €6.9B. FY net profit target raised to above €11.5B before extraordinary charges, and a €4.5B interim dividend is to be paid by year-end.

GEA Group Q3 (reported): adjusted EPS €0.87 against consensus €0.91, revenue €1.46B against €1.48B, adjusted EBITDA €260.9M against €263.6M, orders €1.65B against €1.50B consensus. FY guidance was confirmed.
Hannover Re Q3 (reported): net income €695M against consensus €638M and EBIT €980M against €907M. FY net income guidance of at least €2.7B was confirmed.
Kingspan 9M (reported): sales €7.6B, +10% y/y, with Q3 up 16%. FY trading profit guidance of about €1.15B was confirmed and about €1.47B is expected in 2027.
Almirall 9M (reported): net sales +8.3% to €889.2M, EBITDA +22.7% to €221.7M. FY guidance of 9-12% net sales growth was reiterated.
Eramet: confirmed FY adjusted EBITDA target of €540-610M and capex of €250-290M.

Interpolated annualized core is expected to rise 0.15 pp. The BLS is not expected to publish an annualized print because of last year's government shutdown data gap.

risk_factors: Nvidia CEO leadership uncertainty and tighter scrutiny of tech exports to China.
Fragile US/Iran diplomacy, with Rubio and Trump sending conflicting signals and energy prices swinging.
Inflation and rate risk: an 80% priced December hike from both the Fed and the ECB, and Eurozone inflation at 4.0%.
Regulators are scrutinizing AI and data center financing, with the BoE and ECB reviewing bank lending.
Doubts over AI spending sustainability after the US midterms, per the Nikkei analysis of Japanese manufacturers.
Fading weak-yen windfalls for Japanese exporters.
UK recovery vulnerable to further energy shocks, per KPMG.
vol_and_positioning: The volatility index fell 22.31% to 19.92 on Monday.
The AI trade rebounded on cleaner positioning after last week's aggressive selling.
S&P breadth was the most positive since November 2025, with gainers outnumbering decliners by nearly 6:1.
geopolitical: US/Iran diplomacy: Trump said further strikes on Iran are 'highly unlikely'. Rubio said indirect talks have not been productive. Iran says the Strait of Hormuz can be reopened in two days if its demands are met, and Qatar's PM was to meet Trump and Vance in Washington.

Allegations that Nvidia CEO Huang has a relationship with a woman the US believes is a Chinese intelligence asset. China called it 'baseless smears', and House Republicans want Huang to brief lawmakers.
The Democrat victory in the US midterms, with Democrats assuming control of Congress in January and vowing to investigate Nvidia.
The New Zealand election is inconclusive, with a right-bloc lead and the Opportunity party possibly a kingmaker.
UniCredit expects to take control of Commerzbank by end-November, with ECB approval already received.
cross_bank_references: Citi said a much larger and sustained fall in energy prices is needed to take out a December ECB hike.
BofA highlighted that energy price curves still matter for March ECB rate hike risk.
JPMorgan assessed a US listing for ACS or Hochtief as more likely than one for Turner alone.

tension_points.bear_case: Eurozone inflation is at 4.0%, ECB speakers are hawkish, and Citi says a much larger, sustained energy fall is needed to remove a December ECB hike. About 80% of a hike is priced for both the Fed and the ECB.

tension_points.bear_case: The Democrat midterm win and data center scrutiny raise doubts about AI spending, and the BoE and ECB are reviewing data center lending.
